actual_scope: Can the odd gate scalars 1/3 and 1/5 (a declared change of the native scalar alphabet from dyadic to A = Z[1/2, 1/3, 1/5], with a prefix certificate S = 225) improve the complete signed invoice of the word of #6931?
scope_change_reason: Same native construction, per-port root pair, block-diagonal caller (78 roles, 18 joint contacts), A6 declaration and BIT line as #6931; the word changes (67,079 events, 1451 public registers: ten more helper registers and 39 merged stops, counted against the #6931 word) and the scalar alphabet is changed as a declared framework change: 3,001 odd divisions (59 SCALE, 2,942 ADD), 6,002 scans per call priced separately, S = 225 on every prefix row and pre-ADD product, 3-adic and 5-adic heights 2 and 2. Correctness rests on the exact replay of the final word, the odd verifier with its rejection controls, a second replay mod 2^61-1 with mutants, the replay as streams over F_p[i], an integer run of one column with generic frames (every division exact; a truncated child return rejected at event 26563), the native chart-change maps (3,230) and the joint caller. Exactness is conditional on exact child returns. 20 of the 39 stops come from a reordering of commuting events (no pair sharing a register with a writer changes order); 120 rewritten and 76 tuned events are validated by replay only. Raw counts 962,308,192 / 972,123,664 / 985,187,200, below 10^9; with the second LAMBDA count and the scale at the root 997,747,200, per-input scale 999,836,640. Logarithm power minimum 2222, written 2223 (carrier 153). Peak owned fields 36, 23 owned rises, S = 1520. Gain: +0.470% over #6931.
